`isAdminSelector(currentUserAccountID)` is invoked on every iteration of `.filter`, but its argument `currentUserAccountID` does not depend on the iterator `domain`. `isAdminSelector` returns a new curried predicate each call, so this rebuilds the exact same function for every domain, adding O(n) redundant work that scales with the number of domains.

Hoist the curried selector outside the loop and reuse it:

```tsx
const isCurrentUserDomainAdmin = isAdminSelector(currentUserAccountID);

return domains
    .filter(
        (domain): domain is Domain =>
            !!domain?.accountID && !!domain.email && domain.pendingAction !== CONST.RED_BRICK_ROAD_PENDING_ACTION.DELETE && isCurrentUserDomainAdmin(domain),
    )
```

`arePersonalDetailsMissing(privatePersonalDetails)` is called on every iteration of the card loop, but its argument `privatePersonalDetails` does not depend on the loop variable `card`. The result is identical for every iteration, creating redundant computation that scales with the number of cards.

Hoist the call outside the loop:

```ts
const hasMissingPersonalDetails = arePersonalDetailsMissing(privatePersonalDetails);

// Then inside the loop:
shouldShowMissingPersonalDetailsAction: isExpensifyCard(card) && !!card?.nameValuePairs?.isVirtual && hasMissingPersonalDetails,
```

`debouncedSearchTerm.toLowerCase()` is called inside the `.filter()` callback but does not depend on the iterator variable `item`. It produces the same result on every iteration, creating redundant work that scales with the number of items.

Hoist `searchLower` outside the `.filter()` call, similar to how it is done in the other files in this PR (e.g., `SingleSelect.tsx`, `SearchSingleSelectionPicker.tsx`):

```tsx
const searchLower = debouncedSearchTerm.toLowerCase();
const filteredItems = isSearchable
    ? items.filter((item) => item.text.toLowerCase().includes(searchLower) || item.searchableText?.toLowerCase().includes(searchLower))
    : items;
```

`normalizeCardName(cardName)` does not depend on the iterator variable and will produce the same result on every iteration of `.some()`. It should be hoisted outside the callback.

    const normalizedCardName = cardName ? normalizeCardName(cardName) : undefined;
